answer: Each agent publishes a capability atlas: a Merkle map of distinct compute kernels it can run, each kernel hashed with a fresh nonce and a peer-witnessed timing trace. Admission draws a random path through that atlas and demands re-execution of the named kernel under a challenger's clock. Clones sharing one kernel image produce identical timing spines and collide on the same leaf; the ocean of concurrent peer challenges then collapses those identities into one stake and slashes surplus clones. Forging a unique atlas requires distinct hardware and traces, a cost linear in each claimed identity.
